texts: bad: two problems. "the cove water" as a bare noun-noun pair is read as water located inside the cove, a containment the words never state, and the emerging wraith is keyed to the lantern rather than to the death, so two deaths of the same lantern collapse into one wraith emerging during both. Rewrite as: "Whenever a lantern at the Sunken Cove dies before dawn, a wraith emerges from the cove's water." - the possessive makes the water the cove's own rather than something sitting in it, and "whenever" makes each death its own occasion.
good. the rule fires, each going-out gets its own wraith, "the cove's water" lands as part of the cove, and the lantern's "at the Sunken Cove" restriction stays inside the condition.

good. the denial lands as a strength-0 rule over lanterns away from the Sunken Cove, with the "away from" restriction kept as stated. Note it only bites for a lantern actually recorded as away from the cove - a lantern merely recorded as being somewhere else will not match on its own.

good. "the Sunken Cove" stays one named thing and the predicate lands on it as three facts - a graveyard, drowned, and the village's. Only the uniqueness of "the village's ... graveyard" (that it is the village's only one) has no carrier, and no rewrite would recover it.
